written:
## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. Technology and AI-linked chip stocks led the selloff, and volatility jumped. Dip-buyers pushed the Nasdaq back up afterward.

## 2. What moved and why
**1. AI trade unwinds and volatility spikes**
Why it happened: Fears of a slowdown in data center construction after sweeping Democratic wins in Congress and key governorships drove the rout. Chipmakers took the worst of it.
Why it matters: VIX jumped as much as 70%, to its highest level in seven months, so risk budgets are tighter heading into the week.

**2. Yields ease, but a December Fed hike stays in play**
Why it happened: The 10-year yield fell toward two-month lows as stocks sold off, and investors moved into government bonds.
Why it matters: Polymarket puts about a 77% chance on a December Fed hike after October payrolls rose 165,000 against a forecast near 65,000. Bond buyers and the Fed are reading the economy differently.

**3. Loonie slides on weak jobs data**
Why it happened: Canada shed jobs for a third straight month, cooling expectations for Bank of Canada hikes. Equity-market stress added to the pressure.
Why it matters: Swap-implied odds of a December BoC hike dipped to 35% from 40%. Canada and the US are moving in opposite directions.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Strathcona Resources → Greenfire Resources.** (C$2.7). The deal is valued at about C$2.7-2.9 billion including net debt. It combines two Alberta heavy-oil producers already controlled by the same sponsor.
- **Merger: Marvell → Lumentum.** ($115 billion). The implied enterprise value is $115 billion. It is an all-stock deal pairing Marvell's chips with Lumentum's optical technology for AI data centers.
- **Financing: Blackstone-led group, with four Canadian pension funds → Mitsubishi's LNG Canada holding company.** (US$3.1 billion). The group is investing US$3.1 billion for a 49.9% non-controlling stake. Mitsubishi stays in control of its LNG offtake.

## 3. What's coming today
- 9:00 ET: Constellation Energy earnings call. Read on data-center power demand.
- 10:00 ET: US September wholesale inventories. Minor data.
- 10:30 ET: BoC Market Participants Survey for Q3. Shows rate expectations among dealers.
- 11:00 ET: NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations. Tracks inflation expectations.
- About 12:25 ET: BoE Governor Bailey speaks. A global rates signal.
- 1:00 p.m. ET: US Treasury sells $58B of 3-year notes. Tests demand for bonds.
- Through the day: Fed speakers. Clues on a December hike.
- After the close: Take-Two (call 4:30 p.m.) and Skydance (5:00 p.m.), plus Occidental Petroleum.
- Tomorrow, 8:30 ET: US October CPI, the week's key release.

## 4. Canada corner
- Greenfire jumped 36% after Strathcona's offer.
- AMD disclosed it will pay about US$2.9 billion for Toronto chip startup Taalas, one of the largest Canadian tech takeovers.
- The unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, making a BoC hike harder to justify.
- A Canadian dollar near 1.41 per US dollar raises costs for Canadian importers.

## 5. The takeaway
If someone asks you about markets today: the AI-led selloff and the VIX spike tightened risk appetite, yet a December Fed hike is still mostly priced in. CPI is the next test.
Consulting angle: The AI scare shows the risk of depending on data-center spending. Suppliers should stress-test their revenue under slower capex and diversify customers, while buyers like Marvell must prove synergies justify the dilution.
Accounting angle: In an all-stock deal like Marvell-Lumentum, the acquirer measures consideration at the fair value of shares issued at closing and books goodwill and intangibles. Auditors would focus on those valuations and on impairment risk if AI-linked share prices stay weak.

stories.full:
Stocks rallied Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. The gains reversed Thursday. The Dow lost more than 1,800 points and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%, closing in correction territory. It was the S&P 500's worst day since April 2025.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sank more than 11%, and money rotated toward sectors that had lagged. AMD fell about 15% and Qualcomm about 13%. The S&P 500 erased all of its gains since July 1. The equal-weight index fell less, showing the damage was concentrated in the biggest names.

The Nasdaq rebounded Friday as some investors bought the dip in chip stocks. For the week the Nasdaq lost 3.4% and the S&P 500 fell 2.7%. Winners were the lagging sectors that investors rotated into. Losers were AI hardware and crypto-linked stocks.

Next up: October CPI and PPI, plus CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco earnings. These will test whether AI spending plans still hold.

stories.title: 2. Yields ease, but a December Fed hike stays in play
stories.why_happened: The 10-year yield fell toward two-month lows as stocks sold off, and investors moved into government bonds.
stories.why_matters: Polymarket puts about a 77% chance on a December Fed hike after October payrolls rose 165,000 against a forecast near 65,000. Bond buyers and the Fed are reading the economy differently.
stories.full:
The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with hawkish undertones citing a strong economy and elevated inflation. The next decision is December 8-9.

The jobs beat, 4.1% unemployment and firm pay growth leave little reason for the Fed to pause. Even so, Treasury yields finished the week lower, a split between resilient fundamentals and demand for safe assets. Crude has also swung on Iran headlines. Oil fell on hopes of a US-Iran deal, which helps the inflation outlook.

Tuesday's CPI is the next test. Headline inflation is expected to ease to 0.3% from 0.6%, with core at 0.2%. A hot print would firm up hike odds. A soft one would strengthen the case that the energy shock is fading. Borrowers with floating-rate debt lose if hikes come. Savers and short-duration bond holders gain.

stories.title: 3. Loonie slides on weak jobs data
stories.why_happened: Canada shed jobs for a third straight month, cooling expectations for Bank of Canada hikes. Equity-market stress added to the pressure.
stories.why_matters: Swap-implied odds of a December BoC hike dipped to 35% from 40%. Canada and the US are moving in opposite directions.
stories.full:
Employment fell 4,700 in October and unemployment rose to a six-month high of 6.7%, against an expected gain of 13,600 jobs. Scotiabank strategists said volatility in equities overshadowed most other drivers, with weak Canadian and strong US jobs data adding a further nudge lower.

Earlier in the week the loonie had been strong. USD/CAD hit a seven-week low near 1.3930 on Wednesday. The reversal shows how quickly sentiment shifted. The gap between Canadian and US two-year yields widened to about 139 basis points. The BoC and finance ministry also unveiled a five-year policy framework Thursday, keeping the 2% inflation target.

A weaker loonie helps exporters with US-dollar revenue. It hurts importers and Canadians holding unhedged US assets. Watch today's BoC survey and Tuesday's BoC meeting minutes.

deals.why: The group is investing US$3.1 billion for a 49.9% non-controlling stake. Mitsubishi stays in control of its LNG offtake.
deals.full:
Strathcona's offer is a choice. Greenfire holders can take 0.25 Strathcona shares, worth C$9.09 per share and a 15% premium, or C$11.00 in cash, a 39% premium. Waterous Energy Fund owns 72% of Greenfire and 57% of Strathcona and will elect shares. Strathcona says Greenfire's C$2.8 billion of tax pools could save about C$400 million of cash tax over four years. Closing is expected in late January 2027.

Marvell's offer is a fixed exchange ratio. Each Lumentum share converts into 4.5 Marvell shares, leaving Marvell holders with about 67% of the combined company. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028. Marvell shares ended almost 13% lower on the announcement day. The all-stock structure means the deal's value moves with Marvell's share price.

Mitsubishi is selling a minority stake in the holding company for its 15% LNG Canada interest. It gives Mitsubishi capital without giving up control. For pensions, it is long-dated, contracted infrastructure income.

Together, the deals show large strategic AI consolidation and steady Canadian energy and infrastructure activity.
